record.paper_title: Four nucleon systems: a zoom to the open problems in nuclear interaction
record.original_question: How should nonlocal INOY or Doleschall two-nucleon interaction models be modified so that they retain their ability to reproduce two-nucleon observables and overcome the missing three-nucleon binding energy without explicit three-nucleon forces, while also reproducing the alpha-particle binding energy and proton root-mean-square radius? The concrete failure mode is that these nonlocal models overbind the alpha particle by about 800 keV and predict a proton root-mean-square radius about 10% smaller than experiment, suggesting that the interactions are too soft and may need increased short-range repulsion between nucleons.

evidence.quote: They have managed to construct purely phenomenological nonlocal NN forces (called INOY), which are able to overcome the lack of binding energy in three-nucleon systems, without explicitly using 3NF and still reproducing 2N observables.

In contrary to 3N system, experimental value of α-particle binding energy is overestimated by ∼ 800 keV. Nevertheless this discrepancy is considerably smaller than for conventional local interaction models and is on a par with the result obtained using CD-Bonn NN in conjunction with Tucson-Melbourne 3NF.
In Table 1 one can clearly see that proton r.m.s. radius in α-particle predicted by INOY models is by ∼ 10% smaller than the experimental one.

Such tendency demonstrates that INOY interactions are too soft, resulting into a faster condensation of the nuclear matter. In order to improve these models one should try to increase the short range repulsion between the nucleons.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. A two-nucleon (NN) interaction is a (possibly nonlocal) operator V acting on the relative-motion wave function of two nucleons, designed to reproduce NN scattering phase shifts up to a chosen laboratory energy and the deuteron observables (binding energy, asymptotic normalization, D-state probability constraints, etc.). A class of phenomenological nonlocal NN interactions (the INOY and Doleschall-type potentials) is constructed in coordinate space with a short-range nonlocal part and a long-range one-pion-exchange tail, with the property that, when used alone (without any explicit three-nucleon force), they reproduce the experimental triton binding energy E(³H) ≈ 8.482 MeV in addition to the two-nucleon data.

When such an NN interaction V is used in an ab initio bound-state calculation for the four-nucleon system (the α particle, ⁴He), define:
 • E_α(V) = the binding energy of ⁴He computed from the nonrelativistic four-body Schrödinger equation with V as the only nuclear interaction,
 • r_p(V) = the point-proton root-mean-square radius of the ⁴He ground state computed with V.

The experimental values are E_α^exp ≈ 28.30 MeV and r_p^exp ≈ 1.46 fm (the precise reference value being the one extracted from electron-scattering charge-radius data after standard corrections).

Observed failure. Existing INOY/Doleschall-type interactions V₀ satisfy
 E_α(V₀) − E_α^exp ≈ +0.8 MeV (overbinding by about 800 keV),
 r_p(V₀) ≈ 0.9 · r_p^exp (about 10% too small),
indicating that they are too "soft" at short distances.

Problem. Construct a nonlocal two-nucleon interaction V (of the same general INOY/Doleschall coordinate-space, nonlocal-short-range plus one-pion-exchange-tail form, with no explicit three-nucleon force) such that simultaneously:
 (i) V reproduces the standard two-nucleon scattering observables (phase shifts and mixing parameters in all relevant partial waves up to lab energies of order 350 MeV) and the deuteron properties to the same accuracy as existing INOY/Doleschall models;
 (ii) V reproduces the experimental triton binding energy E(³H) without invoking any three-nucleon force;
 (iii) V reproduces the α-particle binding energy: E_α(V) = E_α^exp within the accepted experimental and few-body computational uncertainty;
 (iv) V reproduces the point-proton root-mean-square radius of ⁴He: r_p(V) = r_p^exp within the same tolerance.

A natural strategy is to increase the short-range repulsion between nucleons in the nonlocal part of V. The question is whether such a modification can be carried out while preserving (i) and (ii), and, if so, to exhibit it explicitly; otherwise, to demonstrate an obstruction.
artifact.category_tag: Nonlocal nucleon-nucleon potentials in few-body nuclei
artifact.status_search_result: Searches indicate that Doleschall-type nonlocal NN interactions (INOY) continue to reproduce the triton binding energy without a 3NF but still fail to simultaneously reproduce the α-particle binding energy and proton rms radius; no published phenomenological nonlocal NN potential is known that solves all four constraints at once. The issue remains an open problem in few-body nuclear theory, with ongoing modern attention shifting toward chiral effective field theory NN+3NF rather than purely nonlocal NN-only fits.

status_evidence.title: Properties of the nonlocal NN interactions required for the correct triton binding energy
status_evidence.snippet: Doleschall examines which features of nonlocal NN forces allow reproduction of the triton binding without 3NF; focus is on 3N, not 4N.
status_evidence.claim: The nonlocal interactions are tuned to 3N binding; the α-particle problem is not resolved within this construction.

status_evidence.title: Influence of the short range nonlocal nucleon-nucleon interaction on the elastic scattering
status_evidence.snippet: Doleschall constructs S-wave nonlocal interactions to improve low-energy binding; alpha-particle radius/binding mismatches persist.
status_evidence.claim: Follow-up work continues to refine short-range nonlocality without simultaneously fitting α-particle radius and binding.

status_evidence.title: Six-nucleon spectroscopy from a realistic nonlocal Hamiltonian
status_evidence.snippet: Realistic nonlocal Hamiltonian applied to A=6 nuclei building on INOY-type potentials.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent applications use INOY-type potentials, indicating the original A=4 deficiency was not fully cured.
